text.p: Olympic Financial Ltd said Thursday it expects net income from operations for the 12 months ending March 31, 1998, to reach at least $1.00 a share before profits that may be derived from retail remarketing.
Earlier, it reported a first quarter loss for the period ended March 31, 1997, of $1.93 a share, after charges, compared with year-ago profit of $0.37 a share.
The first quarter 1997 charges include $1.64 for a change in accounting estimates for recovery rates on repossessed inventory and $0.41 a share for early retirement of notes.
Olympic specializes in purchasing, selling and servicing retail installment contracts for new and used automobiles.
Richard Greenawalt, president, said the company believes that recovery rates are not likely to increase above first-quarter levels, which resulted in the accounting charge.
The company said it also expects to increase the use of wholesale auctions to control inventory size and the costs associated with the operation of retail remarketing.

Going forward, reserves will assume loan loss recoveries equivalent to those expected to be achieved through wholesale disposition of repossessed vehicles -- currently 60 percent of loan balances, compared to 81 percent previously, the company said.
Any recoveries in excess of reserves, which may occur through retail disposition, will be realized as incremental profit as vehicles are sold, it added.
"This change bases our gain on sale assumptions on a lower wholesale recovery rate," Greenawalt said. "We believe wholesale recovery rates to be consistently achievable."

He added the company plans to continue to dispose of a significant percentage of its repossessed inventory through retail channels. In the first quarter, about 65 percent of repossessed vehicle dispositions were through retail sales at selected dealerships, it added.
